note: On Ulla's journey to the Land of Israel, two men from Ḥozai joined him, and one rose and slaughtered the other. The killer asked Ulla: did I act properly? Ulla said yes, and told him to open the cut further. When Ulla came before Rabbi Yoḥanan, he asked whether he had strengthened the hands of sinners; Rabbi Yoḥanan told him he had saved his own life. Rabbi Yoḥanan wondered how such rage could happen in the Land of Israel, since the verse 'the Lord shall give you there a trembling heart' speaks of exile in Babylonia. Ulla answered that they had not yet crossed the Jordan.
why: The Gemara is collecting teachings about anger, beginning with Rabbi Yonatan's warning that the angry are ruled by Gehenna, built on the same verse about a trembling heart. More sayings about anger follow.

people.name: Ulla
people.about: A Sage traveling to the Land of Israel who encouraged a killer out of fear for his own life.

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan
people.about: A Sage in the Land of Israel who told Ulla he had acted to save himself.

terms.meaning: The Jordan River marks the eastern border of the Land of Israel; before crossing it, the travelers were still outside the land.
Encouraged wrongdoers, itself considered a sin.
